blocks.markdown: The Commission is attached to the DICT and headed by a Privacy Commissioner who also acts as Chairman, assisted by two Deputy Privacy Commissioners — one for Data Processing Systems and one for Policies and Planning. All three are appointed by the President for three-year terms and may be reappointed for another three years; vacancies are filled in the same manner as the original appointment. The Commissioner must be at least 35 years old, of good moral character, unquestionable integrity and known probity, and a recognized expert in information technology and data privacy, with rank equivalent to Secretary; the Deputies must be recognized experts in information and communications technology and data privacy, with rank equivalent to Undersecretary.

The Commission may establish its own Secretariat with administrative, technical and other support services, whose members are appointed in accordance with Civil Service Law. A majority of Secretariat members must have served at least five years in a government agency involved in processing personal information, such as the SSS, GSIS, LTO, BIR, PhilHealth, COMELEC, DFA, DOJ or PhilPost.

The NPC combines regulatory, investigative, adjudicative, advisory and cross-border roles: it ensures PIC compliance; receives complaints, investigates, facilitates settlement through ADR, adjudicates, awards indemnity and may publicize reports — acting as a collegial body except where amicable settlement is reached; issues cease-and-desist orders and temporary or permanent processing bans where processing is detrimental to national security and public interest; compels compliance with its orders; monitors government agencies' security measures; coordinates policy; publishes guides and directories of filing systems; recommends prosecution and penalties (Sections 25–29) to the DOJ; reviews voluntary privacy codes; assists and advises on privacy matters; proposes legislation; and coordinates cross-border enforcement. Its administrative powers are distinct from the criminal court's power to convict.
**Answer formula for problems.** State the section, enumerate its elements, apply the facts, and conclude.
